author: Janelle Faignant Correspondent
title: Brandon Festival Singers bring holiday cheer | Local News | rutlandherald.com
text:
Gene Childers started writing his own Christmas songs more than 50 years ago, but without the Brandon Festival Singers he says they might never have been written.
He and his wife Jean started the choir when she was an organist, and he was choir director for the Brandon congregation. In 2022, the group celebrated its 40th anniversary and some members have been with it since the very beginning.
“A lot of singers come from other towns,” Childers said. “We always have people from Rutland, Chittenden, Middlebury, as far north as Hinesburg.”
In 2022, Bernie Carr, executive director of the Brandon Area Chamber of Commerce, who had then been with the group for 30 years said, “One year, (Gene) did all his own Christmas music that he had written himself, which was incredible. It was one of my favorites.”
This year, he’s done it again.
The 43rd annual Christmas Concert by the Brandon Festival Singers will take place at 3 p.m. Sunday, Dec. 14, at the Brandon Congregational Church. The concert features a full program of original Christmas music written for the choir over the years by conductor Gene Childers.
“It’s like writing almost any other song,” he said. Sometimes the lyrics come first, other times it’s the melody. But a notebook and pen aren’t always necessary when the unexpected strike of inspiration hits.
“I’ve been at this a long time so any scrap of paper will do,” he said. “I should have kept some of these over the years because they’re kind of funny, the things you’d end up writing on. I’d be in the car and have an idea and scramble to find something to write on, might be a napkin, might be a paper cup.”
Last year, like most years, the concert packed the church. It’s become a beloved holiday for tradition for many in the area, and this year marks the group’s 43rd year. It was just after it first began that Childers decided to write a new song for the singers every year.
“It just made sense to me that (if) you have a group and they sing well, why not write some music for them,” he said. “That’s how that all began; otherwise, I doubt I would have written Christmas music as much as I have.”
“They’re all telling the Christmas story in some way,” Childers explained. “They’re not secular songs, they’re all sacred and yet presented in a style that’s a little more current and popular.”
“I had done other types of arranging and writing new tunes for old carols, so the choir has done some of those in recent years,” he added. “But these are original lyrics and tunes and arrangements, the whole deal.”
“The music, text and arrangements are my part but, actually, only represent a kind of blueprint or road map,” he said later in an email. “It takes more to make music heard. Those people who truly will bring the music to life are my wife, Jean, our wonderful accompanist; The work of my talented musician friend, Kent Baker, who has made many of this year’s songs look and sound better. Most especially, it is the dedicated, talented singers and musicians who will make the music and the message heard. It is my pleasure and honor to be in their company.”
This popular annual community event is free and open to all by free-will donation, a portion of which will go to charity. Brandon Congregational Church is at 1 Carver St. in Brandon.
